input.summary: This is a USB powered Bluetooth LE sensor node built around an nRF52840, with a meander trace antenna in a keep-out at the top edge. This was a quick review. I ran no simulation because the RF lab is not installed, so I could not check the antenna against the -10 dB S11 target. Two findings matter most. F-001: KiCad reports 21 items shorting two nets (including GND with DEC4, 3V3 with DECUSB, and I2C_SCL with I2C_SDA) and 38 crossing tracks. These could stop the board from working at all. F-002: the antenna feed ANT_FEED crosses a 24.9 mm gap in ground on B.Cu. That makes the feed impedance and return path uncertain, and could detune the antenna. Most of the 351 analyzer results are not reviewed. I only looked at the high severity ones.
top_actions: Fix the shorts and crossing tracks that KiCad reports (F-001) before ordering boards.
Put solid ground under the ANT_FEED line from U3 to the keep-out (F-002).
Measure the antenna match on a prototype with a network analyser, then tune L1, C19 and C20.
Review the medium and low analyzer results that were not covered in this quick pass.

payload.text:
The review is finished and the summary was accepted. This was a quick pass, so I did not simulate anything. The RF lab isn't installed, which means I couldn't check the antenna against the -10 dB target.

I recorded two findings:
- **F-001 (high):** KiCad reports 21 items shorting two nets, for example GND with DEC4, 3V3 with DECUSB and I2C_SCL with I2C_SDA. It also reports 38 crossing tracks. These could stop the board from working at all.
- **F-002 (high):** The antenna feed ANT_FEED crosses a 24.9 mm gap in ground on B.Cu. That makes the feed impedance and return path uncertain, and it could detune the antenna.

Of the 351 analyzer results, I only looked at the high-severity ones. The rest are unreviewed, and the report will show them as such.

Next steps for you:
1. Fix the shorts and crossing tracks before ordering boards.
2. Put solid ground under the feed from U3 to the keep-out.
3. Measure the antenna match on a prototype with a network analyser, then tune L1, C19 and C20.
4. Review the medium and low analyzer results.
